subject: Media on the MLC results and the shrinking trophy
alt: Satish Acharya's cartoon: four TV screens, each with a '24X7' channel logo in the corner and a wall clock above whose hands move forward from one panel to the next. In every screen an anchor in a brown coat and glasses holds a golden trophy, and his speech bubble contains only a lotus symbol. In the first, the trophy is huge, bursting out of the screen, and the anchor is roaring with laughter. In the second the trophy has shrunk and the smile remains. In the third it is smaller still and his face has fallen. In the fourth the trophy is just a tiny figurine on his palm, and the anchor points at it, dismayed. A slip of paper below reads: 'MEDIA ON MLC POLL RESULTS'. The cartoonist's signature in the corner: SATISH ACHARYA.
chutki: The clock moves on and the trophy keeps shrinking. In the morning the anchor laughs, holding a trophy that bursts out of the screen; by afternoon it is half the size, and by evening only a tiny figurine is left on his palm, his face long as he shows it. Each time his speech bubble holds the same thing: a lotus.

Satish Acharya's jab is at a channel culture that announces the celebration before the counting is done. As the MLC results came in, the claim of victory kept getting smaller, but the anchor's words carried the same one symbol. The cartoon asks: when the media turns from news into one party's speech bubble, is it telling viewers the result, or its own hopes?
